sources.title: CEC reports service incident at Tokyo No.2 Data Center on August 5
sources.summary: CEC reports a service disruption at its Tokyo No.2 Data Center at about 11:00 on August 5, 2026 and says service had been restored by its August 6 notice. The incident identifies operating services at the named facility on August 5. It does not date an opening or establish uninterrupted availability; later notices say the affected services were restored in a separate environment.

status_observation_review.basis: Named physical facility service incident identifies operation on the event day; lifecycle operation is distinct from uninterrupted service availability.
status_observation_review.limitation: The later recovery environment is unspecified and is not used to refresh this physical site to August 21 or September 3.

sources.title: CEC says affected services were recovered in a separate environment
sources.summary: CEC says the affected area was isolated and the disrupted services had been restored in a separate environment, with no new service interruptions reported as of August 21. This is recovery context; the notice does not identify that environment as the Sunshine 60 property.

sources.title: CEC closes its incident investigation and confirms continued recovered services
sources.summary: CEC says its investigation found no information leakage from the affected area or related customer systems, and that restored services continue in a safe environment. These are the operator’s reported investigation findings. The September 3 notice does not establish a new physical operating observation at Sunshine 60.

sources.title: CEC Tokyo No.2 facility page and planned October 2026 relocation
sources.summary: CEC describes the Ikebukuro facility as an internet-connectivity hub with two high-voltage power feeds, redundant UPS, gas fire suppression and round-the-clock staffing. The page prominently plans relocation in October 2026. It does not report that the move has been completed or give a closure day; the page itself is undated.

sources.title: CEC opens Tokyo No.2 following the MEX business transfer in September 2010
sources.summary: CEC says it opened Tokyo No.2 on September 1, 2010 after taking over Media EXchange’s data-center business. It described three floors totaling about 2,700 m² within a 60-story building and a 120 Gbps backbone at that time. These are historical specifications and the start of CEC’s operation, not a 2026 capacity measurement or a new building completion.

sources.title: MEX facility page explicitly locates the data center inside Sunshine 60
sources.summary: The legacy operator page names Ikebukuro Sunshine 60 as the data center’s installation environment. It identifies three facility levels and describes redundant UPS, two power feeds, raised-floor cooling and continuous operations. The page is undated; its specifications remain historical location context.

sources.title: CEC identifies MEX service as Tokyo No.2 Data Center
sources.summary: CEC’s current contract index explicitly labels the Media EXchange (MEX) service agreement as the agreement for Tokyo No.2 Data Center. This connects the legacy MEX facility name to CEC’s current facility identity; contract revision dates are not operating-observation dates.

sources.title: CEC relocation plan for Tokyo No.2 customer equipment and leased premises
sources.summary: CEC’s December 2024 plan targets completion of Tokyo No.2 customer-equipment relocation by the end of October 2026, followed by restoration and return of the premises by the end of April 2027. It cites aging equipment, limited expansion and insufficient power capacity. These remain planned deadlines, not verified move or closure dates.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap named Sunshine 60 office-tower geometry
sources.summary: The community map explicitly names Sunshine 60 and provides its tower outline. The selected reference point is the outline’s bounding-box center, inside the named tower. It locates the host building and does not identify CEC’s floors, rack position or a dedicated data-center footprint.

sources.title: Sunshine City office-property access information
sources.summary: The property operator’s office access page and named illustration identify Sunshine 60 within the broader Sunshine City complex near Ikebukuro. The tower is distinct from the World Import Mart building and other buildings in the complex.
